Site Overview
Oliver Crossing is a residential apartment complex located in the Fairfield Court
neighborhood of Richmond, Virginia. The property is divided into two sections: Upper and
Lower Oliver Crossing, both of which fall under the jurisdiction of assigned security
personnel.
Patrol Schedule
● Start-of-Shift Walkthrough: Officers must conduct a full foot patrol of the
entire property (both upper and lower sections) at the beginning of each shift.
● Hourly Patrols: Conduct visible patrols of all accessible areas every hour, including:
○ Leasing office
○ Laundry rooms
○ Maintenance areas
○ Stairwells, breezeways, and parking lots
Duties and Responsibilities
General Patrol Duties
● Ensure all common areas are secure and free of hazards.
● Monitor for loitering, trespassing, or suspicious activity.
● Check that the leasing office and maintenance areas are locked and secure.
● Maintain a professional presence and provide assistance to residents when appropriate.

Laundry Room Protocol
● Weekdays (Mon–Fri):
○ Lock all laundry room doors at the start of shift.
○ Unlock them at the end of shift.
● Weekends (Sat–Sun):
○ Laundry rooms remain unlocked.
○ Turn off lights at the start of shift to discourage overnight loitering.
Incident Response and Documentation
● Stay updated on all calls for service via radio or dispatch.
● Respond promptly to incidents and disturbances.
● Document all incidents, observations, and actions taken in the Daily Activity
Report (DAR).
● Notify site supervisor and property management of any urgent matters.
Jurisdiction and Conduct
● Officers are expected to remain within the bounds of the property unless responding
to an incident involving Oliver Crossing residents.
● Officers must not engage in enforcement actions beyond the property line
unless authorized or in response to an active incident.
● Maintain radio discipline and professional communication at all times.
Emergency Contact – Richmond City Police Department
● Emergency: 911
● Non-Emergency: (804) 646-5100
● Police First Pct: 2501 Q St, Richmond, VA 23223
Firearm and Use of Force Policy:
● Officers must be DCJS-certified armed security personnel with valid
registration and credentials on hand.
● Firearms must remain holstered at all times unless responding to an imminent
threat of serious bodily harm or death.
● Use of force must comply with Virginia Code § 9.1-146 and company policy.

● Any display or use of a weapon must be immediately reported to the site supervisor
and documented in a Use of Force Report.
Armed Officer Protocol (Virginia DCJS Certified)
● Carry valid DCJS armed registration and wear visible ID.
● Firearms must remain holstered unless facing imminent threat.
● Use of force must comply with Virginia law and company policy.
● Any weapon display or use must be reported immediately and documented in a Use
of Force Report.

St. Paul’s Episcopal Church – Armed Security Coverage

Site Overview
St. Paul’s Episcopal Church is a historic religious property located in the Capitol District of
Downtown Richmond. The site is adjacent to Capitol Square and experiences consistent
pedestrian traffic, requiring heightened vigilance and professional conduct from assigned
security personnel.
Patrol Protocol
● Officers must maintain a continuous foot patrol throughout the shift.
● Patrol includes monitoring all entrances, exits, walkways, and gathering areas.

environmental changes.

● Officers must wear a professional dress uniform at all times.

● Monitor for loitering, trespassing, or unauthorized access.

● Report any maintenance issues or safety hazards to the site supervisor.

● Officers must be DCJS-certified armed security personnel with valid

Homemades By Susanne – Armed Security / Parking Enforcement
Company Contact (Unauthorized Parking): No green Tag on Rearview
mirror (see picture below).
Company: On-Time Towing
Phone: 804-933-5436
Site Location: The John Marshall Hotel, 101 North 5th Street, Richmond, VA 23219
Site Overview
The John Marshall Hotel is a historic downtown property with high visibility and public access.
Security presence is focused on maintaining a professional, vigilant posture, ensuring the safety
of guests and staff, and preventing unauthorized activity around the premises—particularly near
the rear exit and designated parking areas.
Pre-Post Procedures
● Check-In Requirement: All officers must report to hotel staff upon arrival for
briefing and coordination.
○ POC (located in Ballroom and Kitchen area)
■ Shelia Clarke (Cell #: 804-306-8274)
■ Sarah Lein (Cell #: 804-591-9269, manager when Shelia is off)
■ Officer Number: 804-775-0021
● Initial Parking Check:
○ Photograph the Spots 4-7 upon arrival. (Rows/spots 4-7 is for
Homemades, row/spot 8 is overflow (green tag still required)).
○ Check for the Green tag hanging on vehicles’ rearview mirror or on
vehicles’ dashboard.
○ If any motor vehicles are found to not have tag, warn the driver to not park
there or they will be towed (if driver is present). The owners of the lot also
have tow trucks patrolling about every half hour to 45 minutes.
○ The only thing that matters is if the car has a GREEN TAG. The officer does
not need to check with anyone about who’s car is who’s. Whether it’s a
guest, staff member, etc., if they don’t have a green tag, they get towed at
their own expense.
○ If any vehicle is unauthorized, notify hotel management and prepare for

tow authorization.
Patrol and Post Duties
Primary Post Location:
● Maintain a high-visibility presence at the rear exit of the hotel.
● Remain alert to foot traffic, loitering, or suspicious activity in the alley or
adjacent walkways.
● The parking lot, the alley and the sidewalk from the front door to the parking lot
should be kept secure. Some people try to park or “wait” in the alley, which is how
the parking spaces are accessed, making the employees unable to leave.
Patrol Responsibilities:
● Ensure no homeless individuals are loitering or encamped on hotel property.
● Monitor the last Four parking spaces throughout the shift to ensure they
remain clear unless authorized.
● Ensure all guests and staff can safely exit and access their vehicles
without obstruction or interference.
● Shelia Clarke and Sarah Lein are usually the last to leave the kitchen area, might
remind the officer that event planners are still in the building.
● Catering Office POC:
○ Kaitlyn McMahon (Cell #: 804-605-2761)
○ Maria Hall (Cell #: 804-387-8749)
○ Officer Number: 804-775-2355
● Either Kaitlyn McMahon or Maria Hall, or both, are usually the last to leave for the
night. After they are gone, the officer can leave.
Tow Enforcement:
● If unauthorized vehicles are parked in restricted spaces:
○ Contact the designated tow company. Homemades would appreciate the officer making a
call on their behalf to On-Time Towing at 804-539-8697, referencing the Fifth Street lot
owned by Charter Realty.
■ Homemades’s contact at Charter Realty is Bill O’Connor, his number is 804-225-
0923, if needed.
○ Document the vehicle make, model, license plate, and time of tow request.
○ Make sure to document all details in DAR or incident report.
Conduct and Compliance

Uniform and Appearance:
● Officers must be in full professional uniform.
● Maintain a clean, well-groomed appearance.
● Remain courteous and composed when interacting with the public.
Firearm and Use of Force Policy:
● Officers must be DCJS-certified armed security personnel with valid
registration and credentials on hand.
● Firearms must remain holstered at all times unless responding to an imminent
threat of serious bodily harm or death.
● Use of force must comply with Virginia Code § 9.1-146 and company policy.
● Any display or use of a weapon must be immediately reported to the site supervisor
and documented in a Use of Force Report.
Prohibited Conduct:
● Officers must not leave their assigned area without supervisor approval.
Incident Reporting
● All incidents, observations, and enforcement actions must be recorded in the
Daily Activity Report (DAR).
● Notify hotel management and site supervisor of any significant events or safety concerns.

Site Overview
Bainbridge Commons is a federally subsidized, family-oriented apartment complex located in
Chesapeake’s South Norfolk district. The property includes multiple residential buildings,
shared green spaces, and two primary parking lots. This is an armed post requiring
DCJS-certified officers with concealed carry authorization. Officers are responsible for
maintaining a visible presence, deterring unauthorized activity, and ensuring safe access for
residents and guests.
Patrol Schedule
● Start-of-Shift Walkthrough: Conduct a full foot patrol of all buildings,
breezeways, stairwells, and common areas.
● Hourly Patrols: Perform visible patrols every hour, covering:
○ Apartment buildings and stairwells
○ Parking lots and drive lanes
○ Dumpster and maintenance zones
○ Playground and green spaces
○ Leasing office and community center (if applicable)
Duties and Responsibilities
General Patrol Duties
● Monitor for loitering, trespassing, or suspicious activity.
● Ensure all common areas are secure and free of hazards.
● Check for unsecured doors, broken lighting, or maintenance issues.

● Engage respectfully with residents when approached; do not provide
property management information.
● Maintain visibility and approachability while remaining alert and professional.
Parking Lot Oversight
● Monitor both parking lots for unauthorized vehicles, gatherings, or safety hazards.
● Ensure clear access for emergency vehicles and resident traffic.
● Report abandoned or suspicious vehicles to property management and supervisor.
Playground and Green Space Monitoring
● Ensure playground areas are free of hazards and not used after dark.
● Discourage loitering or non-resident use of green spaces.
Armed Officer Protocol (Virginia DCJS Certified)
● Carry valid DCJS armed registration and wear visible ID.
● Firearm must remain holstered unless facing imminent threat.
● Use of force must comply with Virginia Code § 9.1-146 and company policy.
● Any weapon display or use must be reported immediately and documented in a Use
of Force Report.
Conduct and Compliance
Uniform and Appearance
● Officers must wear a professional dress uniform at all times.
● Maintain a clean, well-groomed appearance.
● Remain courteous and composed when interacting with residents or the public.
Prohibited Conduct
● Personal cell phone use is not permitted while on duty.
● Officers must not leave their assigned area without supervisor approval.
